data.content_ref: inline:The 'unknown unknowns' argument asserts intuition captures what finite checklists miss, but provides no causal mechanism showing expert intuition is calibrated to those unknowns rather than introducing additional uncontrolled bias. The claim assumes 'compressed expertise' reliably maps to true anomalies, yet never establishes that intuition's hit rate on unknown-unknowns exceeds its false-positive rate in a way that improves expected accuracy on objectively verifiable outcomes. Without that calibration link, the fact that checklists are silent on unknowns does not imply intuition outperforms them; intuition may simply produce untracked errors the checklist would have prevented.
